papers.title: Quantifying Stress Shielding in Dental Implants: A Comparative Finite Element Study of Titanium, CFR-PEEK, and Ceramic Materials
papers.abstract: Background: Stress shielding, which occurs when there is a mismatch between the stiffness of the implant and the bone, can alter load transfer and drive peri-implant bone remodeling, particularly in low-density bone. Methods: We compared the biomechanical responses of one-piece implants made of Ti-6Al-4V, Y-TZP, and CFR-PEEK. We modelled the bone as linearly isotropic in the transverse direction and the implants as linearly isotropic with a fully bonded interface. A static load of 200 N was applied at an inclination of 30° buccal-to-lingual, with the transverse bone bottom faces fully constrained. Results: The peak cortical von Mises stress was highest for Y-TZP (87 MPa), followed by Ti-6Al-4V (57 MPa) and CFR-PEEK (approximately 37 MPa). Peak cortical von Mises strain showed the same relative order of magnitude: 3450 µε, 3103 µε, and 1523 µε, respectively. The stress-shielding factor (SSF) revealed that shielding was present in the mid-apical regions. Y-TZP exhibited the greatest shielding (SSF: 0.844–0.877), followed by Ti-6Al-4V (SSF: 0.380–0.568) and CFR-PEEK (SSF: 0.375–0.437). No crestal shielding was observed (SSF < 0). Conclusions: Overall, implants with higher stiffness increased crestal stress concentration and deepened peri-implant shielding. Meanwhile, CFR-PEEK improved load sharing and produced a more homogeneous mechanical stimulus in low-density bone.

summary_zh.result: CFR-PEEK减少应力遮挡，Y-TZP应力遮挡最严重

summary_en.motivation: To quantify stress shielding in dental implants made of different materials.
summary_en.method: Finite element analysis compared biomechanical responses of Ti-6Al-4V, Y-TZP, and CFR-PEEK one-piece implants with fully bonded bone-implant interface.
summary_en.result: CFR-PEEK implants showed the least stress shielding and more homogeneous load transfer, while Y-TZP exhibited the greatest shielding.
summary_en.validation: The study relied solely on finite element simulation without experimental validation.

papers.title: Analysis and Characterization of Axially Joined Friction-Welded Ti6Al4V Alloy Rods
papers.abstract: The effect of process inputs in the friction welding of Ti6Al4V alloy rods was investigated through the analysis of residual stresses, microstructure, chemical phases and hardness testing of the weld joints. The rods were welded using different combinations of process inputs. The results revealed variations in residual stresses, hardness and microstructure of the weld joints when weld inputs were varied. Peak compressive residual stresses were obtained at the centre of the weld interface, where the grains were very fine. The joints with a greater volume fraction of martensitic grains had elevated residual stress values. The maximum compressive residual stress values were obtained at the weld interface, with high hardness results. A further investigation was conducted to study the relationship between the residual stresses, microstructure and mechanical properties of the weld joint.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文未涉及增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的力学性能或疲劳行为，而是研究摩擦焊接，与研究方向不符。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not involve additive manufacturing of Ti-6Al-4V; it studies friction welding, a different joining process, and lacks fatigue characterization.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究摩擦焊接参数对Ti6Al4V合金棒焊接接头的影响。
summary_zh.method: 通过改变工艺参数进行摩擦焊接，分析残余应力、显微组织和硬度。
summary_zh.result: 焊接参数变化导致残余应力、硬度和微观结构变化，界面处获得最大压应力和高硬度。
summary_zh.validation: 实验测量残余应力和硬度。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the effect of friction welding process parameters on the properties of Ti6Al4V alloy rods.
summary_en.method: Various combinations of process inputs were used to weld Ti6Al4V rods, and the resulting residual stresses, microstructure, and hardness were analyzed.
summary_en.result: Variations in process inputs led to changes in residual stress, hardness, and microstructure, with maximum compressive residual stress and high hardness at the weld interface.
summary_en.validation: Experimental measurements of residual stress and hardness.
